notes: The two καί tokens are decided separately by the English the ASV wrote: the first takes the bare 'even' with καθώς keeping 'as' (rule 82's bare-even arm), the second takes 'also' with οὕτως keeping the whole correlative 'so' (rule 100).
ἔχῃ μομφήν splits, the ASV spelling both elements out (rule 73's contrast).

The final clause expresses no predicate, so the supplied 'do' rides with the subject pronoun ὑμεῖς and heads on 'ye' (rule 56); ἀλλήλων and the reciprocally used ἑαυτοῖς both head on the second word (rule 83).
